title: Winter Practice Period Shuso's Class - Continuing Our Maturity Part 1
speaker: Shin-yu Scott Allen
summary: Maturity is not solely defined by age or societal expectations of adulthood, but rather by a willingness to confront our own limitations and vulnerabilities. This involves embracing our imperfections and being open to growth and change, especially when faced with uncertainty or discomfort. By letting go of ego and cultivating self-awareness, we can develop the maturity needed to truly fulfill spiritual practice and live a fulfilling life, one that is rooted in wisdom, flexibility, and relational depth.

Since this is a discussion with [unclear: "four boys"], I would like to make it truly a discussion.

Be flexible.

Three, real maturity depends on others.

It tends to do that.

They're good in moderation.
One of the things they look at in the book is be strong.

You know what you want and you press on and you go for the gold.
If you do it too much, it's rigidity, and flexibility, and it's not going to work out for you.
So all those things in moderation.
